AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Reality shock is a critical representation of the gap between nursing education and clinical practice and it is important to explore the level of reality shock among nurses. However, there is no relevant instrument to assess the level of reality shock in South Korea.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this is to determine the validity and reliability of the Korean version of the Environmental Reality Shock-Related Issues and Concerns instrument.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A cross-sectional study design was used in this study.

AbstractText.Label: SETTINGS
AbstractText.content: The data collection was conducted in selected 15 hospitals in South Korea.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: A convenience sample of 216 newly graduated nurses participated in the study.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The Korean version of the Environmental Reality Shock-Related Issues and Concerns instrument was developed through the forward-backward translation technique, and revision based on feedback from expert groups. The internal consistency reliability was assessed using Cronbach's alpha, and the construct validity was determined via exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The Korean version of the Environmental Reality Shock-Related Issues and Concerns has reliable internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha=0.91). Exploratory factor analysis revealed five factors including job, relationships, expectations, private life, and performance, which explained 61.92% of variance. The factor loadings ranged from 0.451 to 0.832. The five-factor structure was validated by confirmatory factor analysis (RMR<0.05, CFI>0.9).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: It was concluded that the Korean version of the Environmental Reality Shock-Related Issues and Concerns instrument has satisfactory construct validity and reliability to measure the reality shock of newly graduated nurses in South Korea.
